title: Exhaustive African, Cushite/Nubian (25th Dynasty & Meroe), Ethiopian (Kebra Nagast / Tarika Nagast) & West/North/East African Genealogies

nodes.name: Alara of Kush (Founder of Napatan Dynasty)
nodes.role: Progenitor of the 25th Kushite Dynasty
nodes.notes: Unified Upper Nubia around Napata (Jebel Barkal); revered by all later Kushite pharaohs as their founding ancestor.

nodes.name: Kashta & Queen Pebatjma
nodes.role: Brother of Alara / First Kushite King in Upper Egypt
nodes.notes: Extended Kushite rule into Upper Egypt and installed his daughter Amenirdis I as God's Wife of Amun at Thebes; father of Piye and Shabaka.

nodes.name: Piye (Piankhi) & Shabaka (25th Dynasty Pharaohs)
nodes.role: Kushite Conquerors & Restorers of Unified Egypt
nodes.notes: Piye conquered all of Egypt from Nubia to the Delta; his brother Shabaka preserved the ancient Memphite Theology of Ptah on the Shabaka Stone!

nodes.name: Shebitku & Taharqa (Biblical Tirhakah, King of Cush!)
nodes.role: Greatest 25th Dynasty Pharaoh — Named in 2 Kings 19:9
nodes.notes: Son of Piye; explicitly named in the Bible as 'Tirhakah, King of Cush' who marched to relieve King Hezekiah's Jerusalem from Assyrian Emperor Sennacherib (701 BCE)!

nodes.name: Tantamani → Aspelta → Ergamenes (Meroe)
nodes.role: Last Kushite Pharaoh of Egypt → Founders of Meroe
nodes.notes: Tantamani (son of Shabaka) was the last 25th Dynasty king in Egypt; Aspelta shifted the royal capital south to Meroe (creating the Meroitic script and pyramid fields!).

nodes.name: Queen Shanakdakhete → Amanirenas → Amanitore (Kandakes)
nodes.role: Warrior Queens of Kush (Biblical 'Candace'!)
nodes.notes: Meroe was ruled by powerful Candaces (Kandakes): Amanirenas battled Roman Augustus's legions (capturing his bronze head at Meroe!), and Queen Amanitore corresponds to 'Candace, Queen of the Ethiopians' in Acts 8:27!

nodes.name: King Kikanos of Cush (+ Queen Adoniah) → Menakrus
nodes.role: Cushite Royal House in Moses's 40-Year Reign
nodes.notes: Book of Jasher 72-76 recounts Moses aiding King Kikanos against the rebel Balaam, marrying Queen Adoniah, and ruling Cush for 40 years before turning the kingdom over to Kikanos's son Menakrus!

nodes.name: Ityopis (Ethiopic, son of Cush) → Aksumawi
nodes.role: Traditional Eponym of Ethiopia & Founder of Aksum
nodes.notes: Traditional Ethiopian royal chronicles trace Ethiopia directly from Ham -> Cush -> Ityopis (eponym of Ethiopia) -> Aksumawi (founder of Aksum) -> Malakya Aksum!

nodes.name: Arwe (Serpent King) → Angabo → Gedur → Tawasya
nodes.role: Slayer of Arwe & Ancestors of Queen Makeda
nodes.notes: Angabo slays the tyrant serpent-king Arwe and founds the Agazian dynasty of Aksum leading directly to Queen Makeda!

nodes.name: Queen Makeda (Queen of Sheba / Saba / Bilqis)
nodes.era: c. 10th c. BCE trad. (1 Kings 10 / Kebra Nagast)
nodes.role: Sovereign of Aksum & Sheba / Mother of Menelik I
nodes.notes: Journeys from Aksum/Sheba to Jerusalem to test King Solomon's wisdom; bears Menelik I, uniting the lineages of Judah/Israel, Saba/Arabia, and Cush/Ethiopia!

nodes.name: Zagduru → Bazen → Emperor Ezana & King Kaleb of Aksum
nodes.role: First Christian Emperor of Aksum (c. 330 CE)
nodes.notes: King Bazen reigned at the turn of the 1st century CE; Emperor Ezana converted Aksum to Christianity (c. 330 CE) and conquered Meroe; King Kaleb (Ella Atsbeha) campaigned in Himyar/Yemen!

nodes.name: Mara Takla Haymanot → Emperor Gebre Mesqel Lalibela (Zagwe)
nodes.role: Carver of Rock-Hewn Churches (Trad. Line of Moses & Zipporah)
nodes.notes: Ethiopian Zagwe chronicles trace the Zagwe kings to a daughter of the Aksumite line AND traditionally claim descent from Moses & Zipporah! Lalibela carved the 11 monolithic churches of 'New Jerusalem'.

nodes.name: Yekuno Amlak → Zara Yaqob → Menelik II → Haile Selassie I
nodes.role: Continuous Solomonic Emperors of Ethiopia
nodes.notes: Yekuno Amlak restored the Solomonic Dynasty in 1270 CE; continued through Zara Yaqob, Menelik II (victor at Adwa), down to Haile Selassie I (225th ruler from Menelik I!).

nodes.name: Olodumare → Obatala & Oduduwa (Progenitor of the Yoruba)
nodes.role: Founding Ancestor of Yoruba & Benin Kingdoms
sources: Samuel Johnson History of the Yorubas
nodes.notes: In indigenous Ifa cosmology, Olodumare sends Obatala and Oduduwa to establish Ile-Ife (cradle of humanity). A later 19th-c. syncretic oral chronicle (Samuel Johnson) compares Oduduwa's eastern migration to 'Lamurudu' (Nimrod) from the East!

nodes.name: Okanbi (Son of Oduduwa)
nodes.role: Father of the 7 Crowned Yoruba Monarchs
nodes.notes: Only son of Oduduwa in core Ife genealogy; father of 7 royal children who founded the major Yoruba kingdoms and the Benin dynasty.

nodes.name: Bayajidda (Abuyazidu of Baghdad) + Queen Daurama → Bawo
nodes.role: Progenitor of the 7 Hausa Bakwai Kingdoms
nodes.notes: Prince Bayajidda journeys from Baghdad across Bornu to Daura (Nigeria), slays the well-serpent Sarki, weds Queen Magajiya Daurama, and sires Bawo — father of the 7 Hausa Bakwai states (Daura, Kano, Katsina, Zaria, Gobir, Rano, Biram)!

nodes.name: Bilali Bounama → Naré Maghann → Sundiata Keita → Mansa Musa
nodes.role: Founder of the Mali Empire (Lion King of Manden)
nodes.notes: Mande royal griots trace the Keita dynasty from Bilali Bounama (traditionally linked to Bilal ibn Rabah, Ethiopian companion of Muhammad!) to Sundiata Keita (founder of Mali, 1235 CE) and Mansa Musa!

nodes.name: Mazigh → Baranis & Botr → Queen Dihya (Imazighen / Berbers)
nodes.role: Eponymous Ancestor of the Amazigh (Berber) Peoples
nodes.notes: Imazighen ('Free People', attested in Herodotus as Maxyes and Egyptian inscriptions as Meshwesh!). Medieval North African genealogists (Ibn Khaldun) linked Mazigh to Ham's sons Phut/Canaan, branching into the Baranis & Botr confederations and heroic Queen Dihya (al-Kahina).

nodes.name: Kintu & Nambi (Buganda) / Gikuyu & Mumbi (Kikuyu)
nodes.role: First Human Couples of Great Lakes & East Africa
nodes.notes: Kintu & Nambi (daughter of sky-king Ggulu) are the primeval progenitors of Buganda's Kabaka kings; Gikuyu & Mumbi (created near Mt. Kenya by Ngai) are the progenitors of the nine Kikuyu clans (Nyumba ya Mumbi).

nodes.name: Oranmiyan (Oranyan — Founder of Oyo & Benin Dynasty)
nodes.role: Individual / Lineage Member
nodes.notes: Youngest and mightiest grandson of Oduduwa; founded the Oyo Empire (father of Ajaka & Shango!) and fathered Eweka I, founder of the Oba Dynasty of Benin!

nodes.name: Eweka I (First Oba of Benin, son of Oranmiyan)
nodes.role: Individual / Lineage Member
nodes.notes: Son of Oranmiyan & Princess Erinmwinde of Benin; founder of the historic Oba Dynasty of the Kingdom of Benin.

nodes.name: Olowu of Owu
nodes.role: Individual / Lineage Member
nodes.notes: 1st crowned grandchild of Oduduwa (son of Okanbi's eldest daughter).

nodes.name: Alaketu of Ketu
nodes.role: Individual / Lineage Member
nodes.notes: Founder of the Yoruba kingdom of Ketu (Benin Republic/Nigeria).

nodes.name: Onisabe of Sabe
nodes.role: Individual / Lineage Member
nodes.notes: Founder of the kingdom of Sabe.

nodes.name: Olupopo of Popo
nodes.role: Individual / Lineage Member
nodes.notes: Founder of the Popo kingdom.

nodes.name: Orangun of Ila
nodes.role: Individual / Lineage Member
nodes.notes: Founder of the kingdom of Ila-Orangun.

nodes.name: Bagauda (Kano) & Daura
nodes.role: Individual / Lineage Member
nodes.notes: Founding Hausa Bakwai kingdoms descended from Bawo.

nodes.name: Kumayau (Katsina) & Gunguma (Zaria/Zazzau)
nodes.role: Individual / Lineage Member
nodes.notes: Founding Hausa Bakwai kingdoms (Zaria later famed for Warrior Queen Amina!).

nodes.name: Duma (Gobir), Zamna Kogi (Rano) & Biram
nodes.role: Individual / Lineage Member
nodes.notes: Founding Hausa Bakwai kingdoms.
